seoTitle: How to Export Google Calendar to Google Sheets
metaDescription: Pull events from Google Calendar into a Google Sheets spreadsheet automatically with Apps Script, capturing titles, times, and durations.
intro: Compiling a calendar's worth of events into a spreadsheet for tracking or reporting is tedious to do by hand. A simple Google Apps Script can fetch event titles, descriptions, start times, and durations directly from your Calendar into Sheets. This guide walks through setting it up.

steps.heading: Set up your spreadsheet headers
steps.body: Map out the columns you want, such as event title, start time, and description.

steps.heading: Open the Apps Script editor
steps.body: Access the script editor from your spreadsheet's Extensions menu.

steps.heading: Find your Calendar ID
steps.body: Locate and copy the ID of the Google Calendar you want to pull events from.

steps.heading: Paste the automation script
steps.body: Add the code snippet and reference your calendar ID inside it.

steps.heading: Set your date range parameters
steps.body: Adjust the start and end date variables in the script to control which events get imported.

steps.heading: Run and review
steps.body: Execute the script, grant account permissions, and check your spreadsheet for the processed calendar events.

faq.question: Can I limit the export to a specific date range?
faq.answer: Yes, the script includes start and end date variables you can customize to filter which events get imported.

faq.question: Do I need to know my Calendar ID beforehand?
faq.answer: Yes, you'll need to locate and copy your Google Calendar ID so the script knows which calendar to pull events from.

faq.question: Will this update automatically as new events are added?
faq.answer: Running the script again will pull the current state of your calendar, though ongoing automatic syncing would require setting up a recurring trigger.

faq.question: What details does the export capture?
faq.answer: The script is designed to fetch event titles, descriptions, start times, and durations into your spreadsheet.
